Learned advocate appearing on behalf of the appellants as well as learned advocate appearing on behalf of the Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. are present.

None appears on behalf of the United India Insurance Company Ltd.
Learned advocate appearing on behalf of the appellants has submitted the letter showing service of notice upon the United Insurance Company Ltd., the same is taken on record.

This appeal is directed against the judgment passed by learned Additional District Judge, Motor Accident Claim Tribunal, Burdwan in connection M.A.C Case No. 67 of 2002, (30/2001, 173/2001)
under Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act, whereby learned Judge awarded compensation to the tune of Rs. 1,60,000/- directing both the Insurance Companies to bear the compensation 80,000/-
each.

entities.text: Additional District Judge, Motor Accident Claim Tribunal, Burdwan
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The claim petition under Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act was taken up on account death Swastik Dhua, who was proceeding towards Durgapur with his motor cycle.
At that the time one Truck bearing No. WBP/833 coming from Burdwan side with abnormal speed with rash and negligent manner moved to wrong side and dashed the motor cycle.
Both the pillion riders succumbed to injuries on the spot.
After the accident information was lodged at Galsi Police Station, where specific case was started being Galsi P.S. Case No. 152/2000 under Sections 279/305/427 of Indian Penal Code.

The claimants filed an application under Section 163A of the Motor Vehicle Act claming Smt. Rina Dhua & Anr vs United India Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors on 16 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175595832/
1 compensation of Rs.3,000,00/-
Both the Insurance Companies contested the claim petition by filing their respective written objection denying all averments of the claim petition contending, inter alia, claimants are not entitled to any compensation as prayed for.
In course of trial mother (Rina Dhua) of the deceased was examined as PW-1, who corroborated all contents of the claim petition.
The issue raised in this appeal only with regard to the enhancement of compensation.
Mr. Krishanu Banik, learned advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant has submitted before this court that learned Tribunal assessed the compensation on the income of Rs.50 per day which cannot be accepted in terms of income of unskilled labour even.
That apart, Mr. Krishanu Banik has submitted that multiplier should be 17 in terms of age of the deceased, but learned Tribunal wrongly considered the multiplier 16 in terms of the age of the parent of the deceased.

entities.text: Rina Dhua & Anr vs United India Insurance Co. Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Mr. Banik concludes his argument submitting that learned Tribunal did not impose any interest in terms of Section 171 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

In opposition to that, learned advocate appearing on behalf of the Oriental Insurance Company Limited has supported the judgment passed by the learned Tribunal submitting, inter alia, that income of the deceased was assessed by the Tribunal in terms of avocation of the deceased at the time of hearing.
On careful perusal of the evidence together with FIR and Postmortem report, from the record, I do not find any reason to discuss further on the issue of accidental death of Swastik Dhua by involvement of two vehicles insured with Insurance Companies/respondents.
Learned Tribunal assessed the compensation in terms of income of Rs.50 per day which, in my opinion, was not at all justified even in the case of death of unskilled labour.
In the aforesaid view of the matter, I am of the opinion, that Rs.2000/- per month should considered as income of the deceased who was a boy of 21 years and a student of Bachelor of Arts (Honours).
So far as multiplier is concerned learned Tribunal erred in taking multiplier 16 in terms of age of the parent while multiplier should be assessed in terms of age of deceased.
Therefore, the multiplier should have been 17.
There is mandatory provision of Section 171 of the Motor Vehicles Act for imposing interest on the compensation amount from the date of filing of the application.

In the aforesaid facts and circumstances I propose to reassess the compensation as follows:

2

1. Monthly Income be assessed as Rs. = Rs.2,000/-
2.

Annual Income be assessed as = Rs. 24,000/-
(Rs.2000/- x 12) 3.1/3rd deduction on account of own personal living expenses (Rs.24,000- Rs.8,000/-)= Rs.16,000/-
4. Multiplier as per age of 17 = Rs.2,72,000/-
(Rs.16,000//X17)

5 . General damages =Rs. 4,500/-
_______________ 6. Total Compensation Rs. 2,76,500/-
Therefore, claimants are entitled to get compensation to the tune of Rs. 2,76,500/-.
Both the Insurance Companies have to deposit of Rs.1,38,250/- each along with interest.
It appears from the record that United India Insurance Co. Ltd. already deposited Rs.80,000/- and the amount was withdrawn by the claimants.

United India Insurance Co. Ltd. is directed to pay Rs.58,250/- along with interest at the rate of 6%
per annum from the date (30.04.2001) of filing of the claim application till the date of deposit thereof before the office of Registrar General of this Court.

Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. is directed to deposit the amount of Rs.1,38,250/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date (30.04.2001) of filing of the claim application till the date of deposit thereof before the office of Registrar General of this Court.
Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. is directed to make all payment as mentioned above after deduction of the amount awarded by the Tribunal, if paid.
Both the Insurance Companies are directed to deposit the amount mentioned above within six weeks from the date before the office of Registrar General of this Court.
Learned Registrar General is requested to disburse all amount among the claimants in equal share on proper identification and proof.
With the aforesaid observation FMA 3030 of 2002 stands disposed.
Pending applications, if there be any, also stand disposed of.
